results.question: What is the total number of employees by role at each mining site in the Western US?

results.baseline_sql:
SELECT
  T1.name,
  T3.role,
  COUNT(T2.id)
FROM mining_sites AS T1
INNER JOIN employees AS T2
  ON T1.id = T2.site_id
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    role,
    site_id
  FROM employees
  WHERE
    site_id IN (
      SELECT
        id
      FROM mining_sites
      WHERE
        location = 'Western US'
    )
) AS T3
  ON T2.role = T3.role AND T2.site_id = T3.site_id
GROUP BY
  T1.name,
  T3.role;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT T1.name, T2.role, COUNT(*) FROM mining_sites AS T1 INNER JOIN employees AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.site_id WHERE T1.location = 'Western US' GROUP BY T1.name, T2.role;

results.question: What is the percentage change in the number of tourists visiting Japan from India between March and April?
results.gold_sql: SELECT (SUM(number_of_tourists) - LAG(SUM(number_of_tourists)) OVER (PARTITION BY visitor_country ORDER BY date)) / LAG(SUM(number_of_tourists)) OVER (PARTITION BY visitor_country ORDER BY date) * 100.0 as percentage_change FROM tourism WHERE host_country = 'Japan' AND visitor_country = 'India';
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN date = '2022-04-01' THEN number_of_tourists ELSE NULL END) - SUM(CASE WHEN date = '2022-03-01' THEN number_of_tourists ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(CASE WHEN date = '2022-03-01' THEN number_of_tourists ELSE NULL END)
FROM tourism
WHERE
  host_country = 'Japan' AND visitor_country = 'India' AND date IN ('2022-03-01', '2022-04-01')
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN date = '2022-04-01' THEN number_of_tourists ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) - SUM(CASE WHEN date = '2022-03-01' THEN number_of_tourists ELSE 0 END) AS change_in_tourists FROM tourism WHERE host_country = 'Japan' AND visitor_country = 'India' AND date IN ('2022-03-01', '2022-04-01')

results.question: Who has the highest number of wins as a coach for each team in a season?
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.TeamID, c.CoachName, COUNT(CASE WHEN h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) + COUNT(CASE WHEN a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) AS Wins FROM Coach c LEFT JOIN Match h ON c.TeamID = h.HomeTeamID AND h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' LEFT JOIN Match a ON c.TeamID = a.AwayTeamID AND a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' GROUP BY c.TeamID, c.CoachName ORDER BY Wins DESC;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT T1.CoachName, T3.CoachName, COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS HomeWins, COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' AND T2.AwayTeamID = T1.TeamID THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS AwayWins
FROM Coach AS T1 JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.TeamID = CASE WHEN T2.HomeTeamID = T1.TeamID THEN 1 ELSE 0 END JOIN Coach AS T3 ON T3.TeamID = T2.HomeTeamID
WHERE T2.HomeTeamID = T1.TeamID OR T2.AwayTeamID = T1.TeamID
GROUP BY T1.CoachID, T1.CoachName
ORDER BY T1.CoachName
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT
  T1.CoachName,
  T1.TeamID,
  COUNT(CASE
    WHEN T2.HomeTeamID = T1.TeamID AND T2.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1
    WHEN T2.AwayTeamID = T1.TeamID AND T2.HomeTeamResult = 'Loss' THEN 1
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS WinCount
FROM Coach AS T1
LEFT JOIN Match AS T2
  ON T1.TeamID = T2.HomeTeamID OR T1.TeamID = T2.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY
  T1.CoachName,
  T1.TeamID
ORDER BY
  WinCount DESC

results.question: Identify attorneys who have never handled cases in the 'West' region but have in the 'North' or 'South'.

SELECT T1.attorney_id
FROM attorney_regions AS T1
JOIN handled_cases AS T2
  ON T1.attorney_id = T2.attorney_id
WHERE
  T1.region IN ('North', 'South') AND T1.attorney_id NOT IN (
    SELECT attorney_id
    FROM attorney_regions
    WHERE
      region = 'West'
  ) GROUP BY
  T1.attorney_id
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT T1.attorney_id FROM attorney_regions AS T1 INNER JOIN handled_cases AS T2 ON T1.attorney_id = T2.attorney_id WHERE T1.region = 'North' OR T1.region = 'South' AND T2.attorney_id != (SELECT T3.attorney_id FROM attorney_regions AS T3 WHERE T3.region = 'West' AND T3.attorney_id = T1.attorney_id) GROUP BY T1.attorney_id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN T1.region = 'West' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0

results.question: Which team has the highest number of wins in the 'basketball_games' table?
results.gold_sql: SELECT name AS team, MAX(home_team_wins + away_team_wins) AS highest_wins FROM (SELECT name, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score > away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score > home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS home_team_wins, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score < away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score < home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS away_team_wins FROM basketball_teams JOIN basketball_games ON basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.home_team OR basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.away_team) AS subquery GROUP BY name;
results.baseline_sql: SELECT T1.name FROM basketball_teams AS T1 JOIN basketball_games AS T2 ON T1.team_id = CASE WHEN T2.home_team = T1.team_id THEN T2.home_team END LEFT JOIN basketball_games AS T3 ON T1.team_id = CASE WHEN T2.away_team = T1.team_id THEN T2.away_team END WHERE T2.home_team = T1.team_id AND T2.home_team_score > T2.away_team_score OR T2.away_team = T1.team_id AND T2.away_team_score > T2.home_team_score GROUP BY T1.team_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT home_team, COUNT(CASE WHEN home_team_score > away_team_score THEN 1 END) FROM basketball_games GROUP BY home_team ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN home_team_score > away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC
UNION ALL
SELECT away_team, COUNT(CASE WHEN away_team_score > home_team_score THEN 1 END) FROM basketball_games GROUP BY away_team ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN away_team_score > home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC

results.question: What is the difference in the average duration of closed cases between attorneys in the "criminal_defense" department, ordered by the difference?
results.gold_sql: SELECT attorney_id, AVG(duration) - LAG(AVG(duration)) OVER (PARTITION BY attorney_id ORDER BY attorney_id) as difference FROM cases WHERE status = 'closed' GROUP BY attorney_id ORDER BY difference;

results.pipeline_sql:
ite
SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN T1.department = 'criminal_defense' THEN T2.duration END) - (SELECT AVG(duration) FROM cases WHERE status = 'closed' AND T1.department = 'criminal_defense')
FROM attorneys AS T1 INNER JOIN cases AS T2 ON T1.attorney_id = T2.attorney_id
WHERE T1.department = 'criminal_defense'
GROUP BY T1.department
ORDER BY ABS(AVG(CASE WHEN T1.department = 'criminal_defense' THEN T2.duration END) - (SELECT AVG(duration) FROM cases WHERE status = 'closed' AND T1.department = 'criminal_defense'));

results.question: What is the difference in average salary between employees who have and have not completed diversity and inclusion training, by job title and region?
results.gold_sql: SELECT Region, JobTitle, AVG(CASE WHEN CompletedDiversityTraining THEN Salary ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN NOT CompletedDiversityTraining THEN Salary ELSE NULL END) AS Salary_Difference FROM Employees GROUP BY Region, JobTitle;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT
  JobTitle,
  Region,
  AVG(CASE WHEN CompletedDiversityTraining = TRUE THEN Salary ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN CompletedDiversityTraining = FALSE THEN Salary ELSE NULL END) AS SalaryDifference
FROM Employees
GROUP BY
  JobTitle,
  Region;
results.pipeline_sql:
WITH TrainingAverages AS (
    SELECT
        JobTitle,
        Region,
        AVG(CASE WHEN CompletedDiversityTraining = TRUE THEN Salary END) AS AvgSalary_Trained,
        AVG(CASE WHEN CompletedDiversityTraining = FALSE THEN Salary END) AS AvgSalary_NotTrained
    FROM
        Employees
    GROUP BY
        JobTitle,
        Region
)
SELECT
    JobTitle,
    Region,
    AvgSalary_Trained,
    AvgSalary_NotTrained,
    (AvgSalary_Trained - AvgSalary_NotTrained) AS SalaryDifference
FROM
    TrainingAverages;

results.question: Calculate the year-over-year revenue growth for each restaurant.
results.gold_sql: SELECT restaurant_name, (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) / ABS(LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) as revenue_growth FROM restaurants;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT
    restaurant_name,
    year,
    revenue,
    LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year) AS previous_year_revenue,
    CASE
        WHEN LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ((revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) / LAG(revenue, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) * 100
    END AS revenue_growth_percentage
FROM
    restaurants
ORDER BY
    restaurant_name, year;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT restaurant_name, revenue, year, LAG(revenue, 1, NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year) AS previous_year_revenue, (revenue - LAG(revenue, 1, NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(LAG(revenue, 1, NULL) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year), 0) * 100 AS yoy_growth_percentage FROM restaurants ORDER BY restaurant_name, year;

results.question: What is the maximum consecutive number of days with a financial wellbeing score below 60 for each customer?
results.gold_sql: SELECT customer_id, MAX(consecutive_below_60) FROM (SELECT customer_id, score_date, financial_wellbeing_score, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS consecutive_below_60 FROM customer_scores) subquery GROUP BY customer_id;
results.baseline_sql:
WITH RankedScores AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    financial_wellbeing_score,
    CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_low_score
  FROM customer_scores
),
Gaps AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    is_low_score,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_low_score = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date
    ) - 
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_low_score = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date
    ) AS day_group
  FROM RankedScores
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MAX(streak_length) AS max_consecutive_low_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    is_low_score,
    day_group,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id, day_group ORDER BY score_date
    ) - 
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id, day_group ORDER BY score_date
    ) + 1 AS streak_length
  FROM Gaps
  WHERE is_low_score = 1
) AS Streaks
GROUP BY
  customer_id
ORDER BY
  customer_id;
results.pipeline_sql:
WITH RankedScores AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    financial_wellbeing_score,
    CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS below_60_flag
  FROM customer_scores
), ExtendedScores AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    below_60_flag,
    SUM(CASE WHEN below_60_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ASC
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS cumulative_below_60,
    SUM(CASE WHEN below_60_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ASC
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
    ) AS previous_sum
  FROM RankedScores
), ConsecutiveStreak AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    below_60_flag,
    (
      SELECT
        MAX(CASE WHEN score_date = T1.score_date AND T1.below_60_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * (
          (
            SELECT
              COUNT(*)
            FROM customer_scores AS sub_cs
            WHERE sub_cs.customer_id = T2.customer_id
              AND sub_cs.score_date <= T1.score_date
              AND sub_cs.score_date >= T1.score_date - (
                SELECT
                  (
                    SELECT
                      MIN(score_date) FROM customer_scores WHERE customer_id = T2.customer_id
                  )
                  - T1.score_date
              )
              AND sub_cs.financial_wellbeing_score < 60
              AND sub_cs.score_date <= T1.score_date
          ) - 
          (
            SELECT
              COUNT(*)
            FROM customer_scores AS sub_cs
            WHERE sub_cs.customer_id = T2.customer_id
              AND sub_cs.score_date < T1.score_date
              AND sub_cs.financial_wellbeing_score < 60
              AND sub_cs.score_date >= T1.score_date - (
                SELECT
                  (
                    SELECT
                      MIN(score_date) FROM customer_scores WHERE customer_id = T2.customer_id
                  )
                  - T1.score_date
              )
          )
        ) / (
          SELECT
            (
              SELECT
                MIN(score_date) FROM customer_scores WHERE customer_id = T2.customer_id
            )
            - T1.score_date
          FROM customer_scores
          WHERE customer_id = T2.customer_id AND score_date = T1.score_date
        )
    FROM RankedScores AS T1
    JOIN customer_scores AS T2 ON T1.customer_id = T2.customer_id AND T1.score_date = T2.score_date
  )
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MAX(streak) AS max_consecutive_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    score_date,
    CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_below_60,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date, CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS date_group,
    SUM(CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date) AS running_sum_below_60,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS current_window_count,
    MAX(CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS has_any_below_60_in_window,
    CAST(strftime('%J', score_date) AS INTEGER) AS day_number
  FROM customer_scores
)
WHERE is_below_60 = 1 AND (
    (
        SELECT MIN(score_date) FROM customer_scores WHERE customer_id = T1.customer_id
    ) = T1.score_date OR
    (
        SELECT MIN(score_date) FROM customer_scores WHERE customer_id = T1.customer_id
    ) < T1.score_date
)
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY customer_id;

results.question: What percentage of visitors to jazz events in New Orleans are repeat attendees?
results.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) FROM Visitors WHERE city = 'New Orleans' AND event_name LIKE '%Jazz%') FROM Visitors WHERE city = 'New Orleans' AND event_name LIKE '%Jazz%';
results.baseline_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T1.visitor_id) AS REAL) * 100 / SUM(COUNT(T1.visitor_id)) FROM (SELECT visitor_id, COUNT(*) AS count FROM Visitors WHERE event_name LIKE '%Jazz%' AND city = 'New Orleans' GROUP BY visitor_id) AS T1
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T1.visitor_id) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.visitor_id) FROM Visitors AS T1 JOIN Visitors AS T2 ON T1.visitor_id = T2.visitor_id WHERE T1.event_name LIKE '%Jazz%' AND T1.city = 'New Orleans'

results.question: What is the total number of patients treated with medication and therapy in each country?
results.gold_sql: SELECT countries.country, COUNT(DISTINCT patients.patient_id) FROM patients JOIN medications ON patients.patient_id = medications.patient_id JOIN therapy_sessions ON patients.patient_id = therapy_sessions.patient_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT country FROM patients) AS countries ON patients.country = countries.country GROUP BY countries.country;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT T1.country, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.patient_id) AS total_patients
FROM patients AS T1
JOIN therapy_sessions AS T2 ON T1.patient_id = T2.patient_id
JOIN medications AS T3 ON T1.patient_id = T3.patient_id
GROUP BY T1.country;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT T1.country, COUNT(DISTINCT T1.patient_id) FROM patients AS T1 INNER JOIN therapy_sessions AS T2 ON T1.patient_id = T2.patient_id INNER JOIN medications AS T3 ON T1.patient_id = T3.patient_id GROUP BY T1.country
